brief: A cabinet of three cells with two drawers, one of them shown pulled open.

requirements.evidence: Three full hex bases piece:0,0,0 / piece:1,0,0 / piece:0,1,0 (level 0) form a triangular block of three cells.
Two drawer frames (hex-drawer-frame-notch-mf) at the empty spots beside touching bases: notch:0#-1,1 and notch:0#1,-1, each filling the gap between two bases.

setNotchOpen opened the notch at (1,-1) k4; the drawer at (-1,1) stays closed. check_build shows no rule errors, but the mesh-collision gate reported 'not-run', so the open drawer's clearance is not verified.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell cabinet: three full hex bases in a triangle with two notch drawer frames in the gaps. The drawer at (1,-1) is pulled open; the one at (-1,1) is closed. check_build shows no rule errors (only an info note about cap faces), but meshClash was not run, so mesh clearance is unverified. Drawers would not place on half-base cut faces in this layout, so I used notch drawers instead.

lines.label: M3 x 10 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
